claims.text: After about six months of calling it graphs of graphs of graphs, the idea was given a name this week, Fractal Semantic Graph, defined, and published with the evidence of seven live graphs.
claims.quote: This week we gave it one, defined it, and published the evidence: seven live graphs you can open in a browser

claims.text: A semantic graph gives the edges meaning: every edge is a verb and every verb has a named inverse, so a link reads correctly from whichever end you stand at.
claims.quote: A semantic graph gives the edges meaning: every edge is a verb, and every verb has a named inverse

claims.text: A fractal semantic graph has no privileged level and no single schema; zooming into any node enters a new world with its own node types, verbs, taxonomy and centre of gravity.
claims.quote: A fractal semantic graph has no privileged level and no single schema.

claims.text: Each world is defined by whoever owns it in its own vocabulary, and what connects them is that each is still a semantic graph, so an edge can be drawn from any node in one world to any node in another.
claims.quote: So an edge can be drawn from any node in one world to any node in another, and the walk works.

claims.text: There is no top and no bottom, only the altitude you happen to be looking from and how much definition you choose to load at it.
claims.quote: There is only the altitude you happen to be looking from, and how much definition you choose to load at it.

claims.text: The test for the word: a system that never lets you leave one vocabulary is a single graph or a hierarchy; the fractal property is that on one link you can jump into another universe.
claims.quote: The fractal property is that on one of those links you can jump into another universe.

claims.text: From a risk register's incident fact one can follow named edges into security operations, into the DNS estate and down to a single TCP packet: four worlds, four ontologies, and nobody built an adapter.
claims.quote: Four worlds. Four ontologies. Four taxonomies. One continuous path of named edges between them, and nobody built an adapter.

claims.text: Everything is already a graph, including every file format: a regulation is a graph of articles, a PDF a graph of pages and glyphs, a codebase a graph of packages and methods, a JSON document a tree.
claims.quote: None of them needs to be converted into a graph. Each one only needs its edges named.

claims.text: In a graph a correction propagates instead of being republished: mark one node superseded and every path that rested on it becomes a query, which a document cannot do.
claims.quote: A correction propagates instead of being republished.

claims.text: When the leaf is a word connected to the byte range it came from and the hash of the file that held it, every claim at every altitude above it is traceable to source with no extra machinery.
claims.quote: And provenance comes free. When the leaf is a word, and the word is connected to the byte range it came from

claims.text: The grammar is five rules: every edge is a verb stated in both directions with an inverse; relates_to is banned; properties carry data, never meaning; supersede, never delete; render the answer to a question, never the whole graph.
claims.quote: What none of them gets to change is the grammar, and the grammar is five rules.

claims.text: The banned verb gets the most pushback, but an edge with no verb constrains nothing and cannot narrow a query; the granularity of the verb is the precision of the question you can later ask.
claims.quote: The granularity of the verb is the precision of the question you will later be able to ask.

claims.text: The evidence is eleven altitudes across seven vaults, each a live graph in its own vocabulary, from the law down to the compute instance, every altitude joined to the next by a named edge.
claims.quote: Eleven altitudes, each one a live graph in its own vocabulary, modelled by its own author, and every altitude joined to the next by a named edge.

claims.text: The EU AI Act is parsed from the official XML into 113 articles, 500 paragraphs, 417 points, 180 recitals, 13 annexes and 68 definitions: 1,523 nodes and 1,944 edges, with the SHA-256 of the retrieved bytes at the end of every provenance chain.
claims.quote: 1,523 nodes and 1,944 edges, with the SHA-256 of the retrieved bytes at the end of every provenance chain

value.unit: nodes in the EU AI Act graph

claims.text: The AIUC-1 agent standard as data has 53 controls, 2,788 nodes and 11,610 edges, and its explorer loads two vaults as one graph, one of them the AI Act by article.
claims.quote: the AIUC-1 agent standard as data: 53 controls, 2,788 nodes, 11,610 edges

claims.text: Of 1,126 crosswalks the standard publishes as text, 62 resolve into node identifiers in the regulation graph, and 8 of the 27 articles reached have since been amended, so the crosswalk was written against text that no longer says what it said.
claims.quote: 8 of the 27 articles reached have since been amended, so the crosswalk was written against text that no longer says what it said

value.unit: articles reached by crosswalks since amended

claims.text: Two graphs built by different people for different purposes in different vocabularies, joined by declared edges, produced a finding that did not exist in either of them; that is the whole argument in one number.
claims.quote: That is the whole argument in one number.

claims.text: At the bottom is a threat model that is itself a graph of graphs: eleven linked models from Customer down to Compute, 51 nodes and 179 threats, with one SQL injection traced upward from the method to the revenue it puts at risk.
claims.quote: The zoom ladder, counted: 11 layers, 51 nodes, 179 threats.

value.unit: threats in the zoom threat model

claims.text: Article 45 of the GDPR has not changed a word since 2016 while what it permits has flipped four times, which the atlas draws as a timeline of ruling nodes over one unchanged article node: the text is a constant, its meaning is the graph.
claims.quote: The text is a constant. Its meaning is the graph.

claims.text: The bottom four altitudes of the threat model, environment through compute, are nodes an author placed, not a live import from a CMDB, an infrastructure repository or a cloud account; the connector that emits such an import is not published.
claims.quote: The grammar to receive such an import exists. The connector that emits it is not published yet.

claims.text: Enterprise architecture is a gap: no published graph holds an EA repository joined upward to obligations, the layer between the standard and the system.
claims.quote: Enterprise architecture is a gap.

claims.text: The crosswalks resolve at article level only where the regulation graph has paragraphs, and six of the GDPR atlas's 227 edges use the banned verb because the rule was written after that graph was.
claims.quote: The crosswalks resolve at article level only, where the regulation graph has paragraphs.

claims.text: The agent altitude is a vocabulary of 23 capability primitives, not yet a join: no published graph imports a real permission set and computes the difference against what the operator intended at scale.
claims.quote: And the agent altitude is a vocabulary, not yet a join

claims.text: Naming edges used to be the expensive part and is now the cheap part, because a language model can propose the verb between two nodes faster than a human can type it, so the bottleneck moved to deciding what the graph is for.
claims.quote: Naming edges used to be the expensive part. It is now the cheap part.

claims.text: The schema wars are over because nobody won; the only integration model that survives is one where nobody is asked to conform and everybody is allowed to connect.
claims.quote: And the schema wars are over, because nobody won.

claims.text: Every read key in the article is published on purpose and none of them can write; the grammar in full, with the four situations in which the argument is wrong, is at graphs.sgit.ai, and the vault where the idea was first worked is VoiceDebrief.
claims.quote: Every read key is published on purpose, and none of them can write.

claims.quote: This article is released under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International licence (CC BY 4.0).
